# Tooling History

This document records which tools were considered or used during the Files.com / HackerOne work, how they were used, and what was intentionally not done.

## 1. Remote Desktop Commander

Status: DISCOVERED ONLY / NOT USED FOR SECURITY TEST EXECUTION

What happened:
- Before the user explicitly requested the custom pc-control plugin, ChatGPT inspected the available Remote Desktop Commander tool namespace and saw functions such as read_file, write_file, and start_process.
- No Files.com security-testing action was executed through Remote Desktop Commander.
- After the user said to use pc-control instead, ChatGPT switched to the custom pc-control workflow and did not use Desktop Commander for the Files.com testing work.

Important distinction:
- Tool discovery is not the same as executing a machine-side action.
- No Remote Desktop Commander command was used to click, browse, read local secrets, run Files.com requests, or modify the trial site.

## 2. pc-control custom plugin

Primary execution path used:
ChatGPT -> private GitHub relay -> pc_executor.Executor -> Windows -> durable result -> GitHub -> ChatGPT

Plugin source/instructions used:
- pc-control skill instructions
- Plus agent runbook
- relay protocol reference

Relay repository:
- foto6/help-pc-1
- branch: agent/pc-github-relay

Relay contract:
- request schema: pc_relay.request.v1
- result schema: pc_relay.result.v1

Safety constraints observed:
- no access to protected E:\manhwa
- no passwords, API keys, session secrets, recovery codes, or CAPTCHA data requested or logged
- no coordinate fallback clicking when structured UIA was unavailable
- no blind replay of side effects after unknown outcomes
- durable result checked before claiming completion

## 3. pc-control capabilities probe

Request ID:
chatgpt-dfine-launcher-capabilities-20260930-001

Action:
capabilities.get

Purpose:
Verify that the custom pc-control relay was live and determine available actions before using it.

Observed capabilities included:
- capabilities.get
- action.preflight
- outcome.lookup
- windows.list
- uia.snapshot
- uia.inspect
- uia.focus
- uia.invoke
- uia.set_value
- screenshot.capture
- clipboard.get / clipboard.set
- shell.run
- keyboard and mouse adapters, with coordinate fallback disabled

Result:
- relay_status: completed
- executor_result.ok: true
- Windows executor active
- shell/UIA/screenshot adapters available
- coordinate_fallback_enabled: false
- protected root included E:\manhwa

Security relevance:
This probe established the execution boundary before any local testing-related action.

## 4. windows.list usage for Files.com

Request IDs:
- chatgpt-files-bounty-windows-20260930-001
- chatgpt-files-bounty-status-20260930-001

Action:
windows.list

Purpose:
- Confirm that the authorized Files.com trial browser window existed.
- Confirm the current browser page/title without reading browser secrets.
- Avoid guessing whether the user session was still alive.

Observed authorized browser states included:
- "Not Found · [BUGBOUNTY] foto6 test - Google Chrome"
- "public-b · Folder · [BUGBOUNTY] foto6 test - Google Chrome"

Result:
- successful read-only window enumeration
- no customer site discovered or targeted
- no session/cookie extraction performed

## 5. screenshot.capture usage

Request IDs:
- chatgpt-files-bounty-screenshot-20260930-001
- chatgpt-files-bounty-shot-publicb-20260930-001

Action:
screenshot.capture

Purpose:
- Capture the currently visible authorized Files.com trial window after UIA difficulties.
- Verify the state of the test-user page without using raw-coordinate interaction.

Result:
- screenshot capture succeeded
- one capture returned SHA-256 404be23598443d4967dd373c058df4630e148efc446ed218e128c73c32199dff
- another capture of public-b succeeded and was inspected visually in ChatGPT

Limit:
Screenshots were used as local diagnostic context, not as Burp evidence and not as a substitute for server-side authorization testing.

## 6. UIA attempts

Request IDs:
- chatgpt-files-bounty-uia-snapshot-20260930-001
- chatgpt-files-uia-inspect-20260930-001
- chatgpt-files-uia-publicb-name-20260930-001

Actions:
- uia.snapshot
- uia.inspect

Purpose:
Use structured UI Automation against the authorized Files.com Chrome window instead of raw mouse coordinates.

Observed results:
- uia.snapshot timed out
- one uia.inspect call was blocked because the query had no non-empty selector
- a later name-based uia.inspect attempt timed out

Result:
BLOCKED / NO SECURITY FINDING

Important:
- No raw-coordinate fallback was used.
- No browser session token or cookie was extracted to bypass the UIA limitation.
- No test was falsely reported as completed after these timeouts.

## 7. shell.run usage relevant to audit/control

pc-control shell.run was used for local Windows actions where a bounded PowerShell command was appropriate.

Examples:
- creating the audit directory and Markdown files
- computing SHA-256 hashes of audit files
- earlier D-FINE local tooling work unrelated to Files.com security testing

For Files.com security testing:
- shell.run has not been used to scrape browser secrets, cookies, passwords, or API keys.
- shell.run has not been used to scan arbitrary files.com subdomains.
- shell.run has not been used to exceed the program rate limit or brute force functionality.

## 8. GitHub connector usage

GitHub connector was used as the transport/control plane for pc-control relay requests and results.

Typical flow:
1. create immutable request JSON in relay/requests/<id>.json
2. wait for relay/results/<id>.json
3. verify version, id, action, relay_status, executor_result.ok/status
4. inspect outcome_evidence for side effects

Why:
The current ChatGPT session did not expose a distinct callable Native R22 tool namespace, so the documented Plus relay path was used.

Important:
GitHub was not used to publish vulnerability details publicly.
The relay repository is part of the user's private control workflow.

## 9. Files tool / uploaded policy text

The user supplied the Files.com HackerOne Security Page as pasted text.

ChatGPT used the file content as the authoritative program-policy basis for:
- in-scope assets
- trial-site requirements
- 2 requests/second automation limit
- customer-data stopping rule
- prohibition on testing customer sites
- in-app AI Assistant exclusion
- Burp evidence exclusion
- AI-use requirements
- report requirements

This policy text was not treated as permission to test anything outside the explicitly listed scope.

## 10. Public web research

Web search was used for public documentation and product information, including:
- HackerOne onboarding/resource pages
- Files.com public documentation
- GPU rental pricing/model information in a separate model-training discussion

For the Files.com bounty workflow, public web research was used to understand documentation and expected behavior, not to enumerate or attack targets.

## 11. Browser / DevTools / Burp status

Burp Suite:
- Not used to produce report evidence.
- No Burp capture was submitted or stored in the audit.
- This matches the Files.com policy that Burp-derived evidence is not accepted for reports.

DevTools/fetch:
- Discussed as a possible future method after UIA timeouts.
- Not yet executed as a completed authorization test at the time this history was written.

Browser secrets:
- no cookies/session tokens/passwords extracted by ChatGPT
- no API key has been requested from the user
- user was explicitly told not to paste API keys into chat

## 12. Files.com tests actually completed so far

Completed:
- researcher-created trial environment established by the user
- Standard User tetst1 created by the user
- tetst1 granted Full Access to public-b
- tetst1 not granted access to private-a
- direct browser navigation by tetst1 to private-a resulted in Not Found / permission-style denial
- current Files.com trial window state verified through pc-control

Not completed:
- share-permission bypass test
- cross-folder move/copy authorization test
- API parity authorization test
- any confirmed vulnerability PoC

Current finding status:
NO CONFIRMED VULNERABILITY

## 13. Actions intentionally not performed

- no customer site testing
- no arbitrary *.files.com subdomain scanning
- no brute force
- no DoS
- no phishing or social engineering
- no testing of the in-app Files.com AI Assistant
- no credential/session extraction
- no API-key collection by ChatGPT
- no raw-coordinate clicking to bypass pc-control UIA safeguards
- no persistence or shell establishment against Files.com systems
- no access to customer data
- no claim of a vulnerability without reproducible evidence
